name: Mikel Arteta
source_file: Why Arsenal Are STILL Getting Better Under Mikel Arteta (The Adam Clery Football Channel)

fullbacks.xp_impact: Calafiori leaves left-back to play as an inverted midfielder or join the last line; Ben White combines in the right-side triangle. The left channel he vacates is the target on turnovers

wingers.xp_impact: Tzolis holds the left touchline to be released 1v1 after the right-side overload; Saka combines in tight triangles on the right

pivots.xp_impact: Rice anchors a 2+1 rest defence with Gabriel and Saliba; if he is drawn forward, turnovers find open ground in front of the centre-backs

strikers.xp_impact: Havertz drops deep to drag a centre-back out of the line, then spins into the vacated half-space; second-line runners attack the gap

analysis.heading: Structure: fluid rotations and fullback inversion

points.label: 4-3-3 to a free-form front line
points.text: In possession Arsenal drop rigid positions and rotate players across all five vertical channels. Calafiori often leaves left-back to play as an inverted midfielder or an extra striker on the last line.

points.label: Local triangles, global width
points.text: Saka, Ødegaard, Havertz and Ben White combine tightly on the right, while Christos Tzolis holds full width on the opposite touchline to keep the back line stretched.

points.label: Dragging man-markers
points.text: Havertz and Ødegaard drop into midfield together. When defenders follow, gaps open between the centre-backs for second-line runners such as Myles Lewis-Skelly or Gabriel.

points.label: High press
points.text: Arsenal press from a 4-2-4 / 4-4-2 base, locking passing lanes and forcing long clearances.

points.label: Rest-defence exposure
points.text: When Calafiori attacks centrally or joins the front line, Arsenal rely on a 2+1 rest defence (Gabriel, William Saliba, Declan Rice). A middle-third turnover leaves the vacated left channel open to direct balls.

analysis.heading: In possession: dilemmas between the lines

points.label: Drop and spin
points.text: Havertz drops deep to receive facing his own goal, pulling a centre-back out of line, then spins into the vacated half-space.

points.label: Overload to isolate
points.text: Sustained passing draws the block toward the right before the ball goes through Calafiori to release Tzolis 1v1 on the left.

points.label: Calafiori's vacated flank
points.text: Quick diagonals into the wide channel Calafiori vacates arrive before Gabriel can slide across to cover the 1v1.

points.label: Rest-defence gaps on turnovers
points.text: If Rice is drawn forward, transitions into the space between midfield and the back line leave the centre-backs isolated in open ground.

name: Unai Emery
source_file: This New Aston Villa Are Going to Shock Everyone (Bains Analysis)

fullbacks.xp_impact: In the flat 4-4-2 Rogério was left 1v1 against Savinho; the 5-3-2 fix drops McGinn in as a temporary right wing-back and brings Buendía across to double up on the left

wingers.xp_impact: McGinn tracks overlapping fullbacks into the back line; Buendía tucks inside to cover central midfield while helping on the left touchline

strikers.xp_impact: Jackson alternates dropping to feet and spinning into the channels, isolating centre-backs 1v1 in transition; Manzambi arrives late from the #10 space into the box

analysis.heading: Structure: the mid-match shift from 4-4-2 to 5-3-2

points.label: 4-4-2 under strain
points.text: Unai Emery started in Villa's signature flat 4-4-2 mid-block. Tottenham pushed Andrew Robertson onto the last line to make a five-man front, pinning Villa's back line and leaving left-back Rogério 1v1 with Savinho.

points.label: Switch to a back five
points.text: Emery moved to a 5-3-2, with right midfielder John McGinn tracking Robertson deep into the back line as a temporary right wing-back.

points.label: Tucking in, doubling up
points.text: Emiliano Buendía moved inside to cover central midfield while helping Rogério on the left touchline, removing the wide disadvantage and closing interior lanes.

points.label: Touchline funnelling
points.text: Villa use the sideline as an extra boundary to trap ball carriers once play leaves the central corridor.

points.label: Contain, then jump
points.text: Rather than press high man-to-man, Villa drop into a compact block and only challenge aggressively once the ball is forced into contested wide zones.

analysis.heading: In possession: mobile front two and direct releases

points.label: Jackson–Manzambi pair
points.text: Nicolas Jackson and Nathan Manzambi play as a fluid front two, with Jackson alternating between dropping to feet and spinning behind the centre-backs into the channels.

points.label: Isolating centre-backs
points.text: Jackson repeatedly isolated Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke in 1v1 transition duels, while Manzambi timed late runs from the #10 space into the box.

points.label: Keeper as release valve
points.text: Zion Suzuki's direct long passes bypass a high line to find Jackson early on the counter.

points.label: Flat midfield four
points.text: Back in a flat four, the lack of vertical staggering lets opponents find players in the pockets between the lines.

points.label: Wide overloads
points.text: If McGinn doesn't drop into the back line in time, overlapping fullbacks can isolate Villa's outside backs.

points.label: McGinn's depth
points.text: In what share of defensive possessions does McGinn drop level with the centre-backs to make a back five?

points.label: Jackson's touches
points.text: Are his touches facing goal after channel runs, or back to goal as a dropping link player?

points.label: Suzuki's long balls
points.text: What share of Suzuki's direct passes into the attacking half within five seconds of a turnover are completed?

name: Keith Andrews
source_file: How Keith Andrews' Brentford OUTSMARTED De Zerbi (Bains Analysis)

fullbacks.xp_impact: Lewis-Potter moves from left-back into central midfield for overloads; the left touchline is open if the ball is lost quickly

pivots.xp_impact: Janelt and Sangare alternate dropping beside the centre-backs for a 3v2 in build-up and track opposing midfielders man-to-man; Sangare carries second balls forward

strikers.xp_impact: Kelleher goes long to Thiago and Schade; Thiago and Jensen press the centre-backs while cover-shadowing the opposing pivot

wingers.xp_impact: Schade contests aerial duels against fullbacks and stepping centre-backs, flicking into space for runners; Schade and Anthony tight-mark opposing fullbacks

points.label: Base shape
points.text: Keith Andrews' Brentford play a flexible 4-3-3 that becomes a diamond through the middle in build-up.

points.label: Inverted left-back
points.text: Keane Lewis-Potter moves from left-back into central midfield pockets to create central overloads.

points.label: Rotating pivots
points.text: Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangare take turns dropping beside the centre-backs for a 3v2 in build-up.

points.label: Screening the build-up
points.text: Igor Thiago and Mathias Jensen press the centre-backs while using their cover shadows to block passes into the double pivot.

points.label: Man-to-man midfield
points.text: Janelt and Sangare track the opposing central midfielders, cutting off short options and forcing the goalkeeper long.

points.label: Flank containment
points.text: Wide attackers Kevin Schade and Jaidon Anthony tight-mark the opposing fullbacks to stop wide progression.

analysis.heading: In possession: aerial duels and direct transition

points.label: Target directness
points.text: Goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher plays direct aerial balls to Schade and Thiago, bypassing the opponent's midfield press.

points.label: Knockdown duels
points.text: Schade contests aerial duels with fullbacks or stepping centre-backs, flicking the ball into space for running midfielders.

points.label: Ball carrying
points.text: Sangare collects second balls and drives through midfield, linking with Lewis-Potter on the edge of the box.

points.label: Behind Lewis-Potter
points.text: When Lewis-Potter moves inside, the left touchline is open if possession is lost quickly.

points.label: Physical load
points.text: Man-to-man tracking over long distances tires the midfield late in games, opening gaps in front of the back line.

name: Fabian Hürzeler
source_file: Why Brighton Are The Premier League's SCARIEST Team (The Adam Clery Football Channel)

pivots.xp_impact: A deep pivot (e.g. Groß) drops between or alongside the centre-backs for a +1 against the first pressing line; the double pivot forms triangles with dropping attacking midfielders to circulate

strikers.xp_impact: Presses on the trigger — a back pass to the goalkeeper or a centre-back — then locks onto the nearest receiver man-to-man

wingers.xp_impact: Up to five players flood the penalty box once the opponent commits centrally

fullbacks.xp_impact: Collapse toward the ball-side touchline to trap an opposing fullback; the far side is left open to quick switches

analysis.heading: Out of possession: base block and triggers

points.label: Zonal mid-block
points.text: A base 4-2-3-1 that holds compact distances between the lines rather than chasing, denying interior passing channels when the opponent circulates centrally.

points.label: Sideline traps
points.text: When play goes to an opposing fullback, the block collapses laterally toward the ball side for a local 5v3, cutting off forward options and forcing the ball back toward the goalkeeper or centre-backs.

points.label: Pressing trigger
points.text: A back pass to the goalkeeper or a centre-back is the cue: the whole side steps out of the mid-block together, from zonal cover into an aggressive high press.

points.label: Man-marking
points.text: Once triggered, every nearby receiver is picked up man-to-man. Centre-backs step deep into the opponent's defensive third to follow dropping forwards so target players can't turn.

points.label: Body shape
points.text: Pressing opponents who have their backs to goal forces turnovers or rushed clearances into touch — the video counts 41 danger-zone possession losses forced against Arsenal.

points.label: Close proximity
points.text: Players stay within 8–15 metres of each other, so the ball carrier always has three to five short passing options.

points.label: Build-up
points.text: Deep players such as Pascal Groß drop between or alongside the centre-backs to create a +1 against the first pressing line.

points.label: Middle third
points.text: The double pivot and dropping attacking midfielders form triangles to circulate the ball and pull the defensive block out of shape.

points.label: Final third
points.text: Once the opponent commits centrally, up to five players flood the penalty box to attack the open channels.

points.label: Over the top
points.text: A high line locked into man-to-man duels can be bypassed with direct, aerial balls into the space behind the back line.

points.label: Switches of play
points.text: Committing five to the ball side leaves the far flank open — a quick switch to an isolated wide runner exploits the reorganisation.

name: Xabi Alonso
source_file: Why Chelsea Are SERIOUS Title Contenders (The Adam Clery Football Channel)

fullbacks.xp_impact: Gusto and Hato hold the width; outside centre-backs Lacroix and Acheampong underlap into the front line, and Acheampong and Gusto jump high on the sideline pressing trigger

pivots.xp_impact: Reece James and Lavia form the base of a box midfield with Palmer and Rogers, giving central superiority in the middle third

wingers.xp_impact: Palmer and Rogers play inside at the top of the box; Palmer drops into the half-space a forward-running Lacroix vacates. First targets in a two-to-four-pass vertical release

strikers.xp_impact: João Pedro is a first vertical target in transition, attacking the equal-numbers (3v3, 2v2) situations Chelsea engineer by inviting pressure

points.label: Structural flexibility
points.text: Xabi Alonso's Chelsea play a 3-4-2-1 in possession that drops into a 5-4-1 low-to-mid block without the ball.

points.label: Box midfield
points.text: With Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato holding the width, two pivots (Reece James, Roméo Lavia) and two inside playmakers (Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers) form a central box for numerical superiority in midfield.

points.label: Extreme rotations
points.text: Outside centre-backs such as Maxence Lacroix or Josh Acheampong make deep underlapping runs into the front line. When Lacroix goes high, Palmer drops into the half-space he left, scrambling the opponent's marking.

points.label: Central funnelling
points.text: The front three and midfield screen the central corridors, daring the opponent to go wide to the fullbacks.

points.label: Sideline jump
points.text: A pass toward the touchline triggers a collective jump: Acheampong and Gusto press high into the opponent's defensive third while the other two centre-backs dominate the resulting aerial clearances.

points.label: Direct release
points.text: Rather than linger in build-up, Chelsea go forward to João Pedro, Palmer or Rogers in two to four passes.

points.label: Manufacturing 1v1s
points.text: Inviting opponents to hold the ball and push men forward creates equal-numbers transitions (3v3, 2v2) instead of attacks into a packed low block.

points.label: Stretched back three
points.text: Wide rotations by the outside centre-backs stretch the distances across the back three; quick vertical combinations run through the seams between Levi Colwill and the wide centre-backs.

points.label: Goalkeeper hesitation
points.text: A high starting position plus indecision about sweeping or holding the line exposes Chelsea to transitional cutbacks.

name: Frank Lampard
source_file: Coventry City Updated Tactical Analysis | Can new look Sky Blues shock the Premier League? (Simon Lillibury)

fullbacks.xp_impact: DaSilva and van Ewijk drop into the back five and step out to trap opposing fullbacks; in possession the back three frees them to push high for early diagonal crosses

pivots.xp_impact: Grimes and Torp step to passes into dropping attackers while the back three hold depth; they drop in against crosses, which leaves the edge of the box open

strikers.xp_impact: Awoniyi or Simms receive direct balls to hold up, with Rudoni contesting the knockdowns

wingers.xp_impact: Mason-Clark or Sakamoto are fed from second balls to attack 1v1 out wide

points.label: Back five
points.text: Frank Lampard's Coventry set up in a 5-3-2 that drops into a 5-4-1 without the ball: centre-backs Bobby Thomas, Ethan Pinnock and Joël Amenda, with wing-backs Jay DaSilva and Milan van Ewijk.

points.label: Interior denial
points.text: They pack the box and the half-spaces, limiting open shooting channels through the middle.

points.label: Funnelling to the perimeter
points.text: Coventry concede the outside channels and wide delivery angles on purpose, relying on Pinnock and Thomas to win headers in the box.

points.label: Contain, don't jump
points.text: A containing mid-block rather than an aggressive high press — they defend the middle and defensive thirds and challenge once the ball goes wide.

points.label: Sideline traps
points.text: When the ball reaches an opposing fullback, the wing-back steps out and the near-side central midfielder shifts across to seal the touchline, using the sideline as an extra defender.

points.label: Tracking runners
points.text: Matt Grimes and Victor Torp step to passes into dropping attackers while the back three stay put to protect depth.

analysis.heading: In possession: target release and wing-back overlaps

points.label: Direct to the front line
points.text: Coventry go vertical with direct passes into Taiwo Awoniyi or Ellis Simms.

points.label: Wing-backs push on
points.text: With the back three covering, van Ewijk and DaSilva push high to deliver early diagonal crosses.

points.label: Second balls
points.text: Dropping attackers such as Jack Rudoni contest knockdowns in the final third and feed wingers Ephron Mason-Clark or Tatsuhiro Sakamoto for 1v1s.

points.label: Back-four switch
points.text: When Coventry revert to a back four (4-2-3-1), the wide areas open up — the gap between fullback and wide midfielder allows 2v1 overloads.

points.label: Cutbacks to the arc
points.text: Central midfielders drop into the line to help against crosses, leaving the space outside the box free for late runners.

points.label: Block depth
points.text: Do the wing-backs sit flat with the centre-backs in a back five, or stay in the midfield line during the opponent's build-up?

points.label: Awoniyi knockdowns
points.text: How many direct balls to Awoniyi produce a controlled second touch for Rudoni or Grimes?

points.label: Crosses conceded
points.text: Count crosses conceded from wide and check whether the centre-backs keep an aerial duel success rate above 65%.

name: Pierre Sage
source_file: How Sage's Palace Edge Arbeloa's Fulham | Fulham vs Crystal Palace 2-3 | In-Depth Analysis (Greatest Sport)

fullbacks.xp_impact: The right wing-back pins high while Mitchell starts deeper to draw the opposing right-back out, then attacks the space behind him; the far-side wing-back (Mitchell or Chilwell) crashes the far post

wingers.xp_impact: Pino and Nketiah play as twin #10s in the half-spaces; Pino plays first-time around the corner into the channel, and both drop to collect second balls

pivots.xp_impact: Only two central midfielders cover transitions across the full width behind the twin #10s

points.text: Pierre Sage's Palace play a back three, two central midfielders, two inside #10s (Yeremy Pino and Eddie Nketiah) and attacking wing-backs.

points.label: Asymmetric wing-backs
points.text: The right wing-back pushes high to pin a defender while left wing-back Tyreek Mitchell stays deeper during progression, drawing Fulham's right-back (Timothy Castagne) out to press and opening space behind him.

points.label: Half-space overloads
points.text: Pino and Nketiah operate in the channels between the opposing fullbacks and centre-backs, giving immediate forward passing angles.

points.label: Forcing it long
points.text: On opposition goal kicks Palace mark the short options man-to-man, forcing the ball long.

points.label: First header
points.text: Chris Richards steps up to contest and win the first header against the target attacker.

points.label: Second-ball trap
points.text: Pino and Nketiah drop into central pockets on the flick-on to collect second balls before the opponent's midfield can react.

analysis.heading: In possession: vertical directness and third-man runs

points.label: Around the corner
points.text: Once Pino receives, he plays first-time passes around the corner into the channel.

points.label: Blind-side runs
points.text: Mitchell uses his pace to attack the space behind Castagne, receiving in stride to cross low or finish at the near post.

points.label: Far-post crashes
points.text: When attacks go down the right, the opposite wing-back (Mitchell or Ben Chilwell) attacks the far post unmarked as the back line shifts.

points.label: Exposed midfield pair
points.text: With two inside #10s, only two central midfielders cover defensive transitions across the width.

points.label: Isolated centre-backs
points.text: If the first pressing wave is bypassed, the wide centre-backs can be pulled into uncomfortable 1v1s in the channels.

points.label: Mitchell's starting position
points.text: How deep does Mitchell sit relative to the midfield line during goal-kick build-up?

points.label: Pino's layoffs
points.text: Count Pino's first-time vertical releases into the wide channels after receiving between the lines.

points.label: Second balls
points.text: What share of Richards' won headers turn into controlled Palace possession?

name: David Moyes
source_file: "You can't change him!" | Gavin Buckland Breaks Down David Moyes' Tactics (Royal Blue: Everton FC)

pivots.xp_impact: The midfield four sits tight to the back line to deny any space between the lines

wingers.xp_impact: Double up with the fullback when the ball is played tight to the touchline — the only real pressing trigger

strikers.xp_impact: Left isolated when Everton sit deep after the 60th minute, reducing the counter-attacking threat

points.label: Two banks of four
points.text: David Moyes sets Everton up in a disciplined low-to-mid 4-4-2 / 4-5-1, with the main aim of denying penetration through the middle.

points.label: Conceding the flanks
points.text: Opponents are allowed to circulate around the perimeter and progress wide while the box stays congested.

points.label: Tight inter-line spacing
points.text: The midfield four stays close to the back line so opponents can't find space between the lines.

points.label: Contain, don't hunt
points.text: No proactive high pressing — Everton hold a containing block until the ball enters their defensive third.

points.label: Sideline trigger
points.text: Pressing starts only when an opponent plays into tight space against the touchline, where the wide midfielder and fullback can double the receiver.

points.label: Steady points
points.text: Moyes prioritises risk control and steady away points — Everton have the third-highest away points total in the league this way.

points.label: After 60 minutes
points.text: If the game is level after the 60th minute, Everton lock their shape rather than push numbers forward, relying on solidity to take the draw or nick a goal from a set piece or a counter.

points.label: Sustained box pressure
points.text: Sitting deep for long spells hands opponents repeated second balls and shots from around the box.

points.label: Little transition support
points.text: Defending deep late on leaves the lone striker isolated, blunting the counter.

points.label: Block height after 60'
points.text: How far is Everton's defensive line from their own goal before and after the 60-minute mark?

points.label: Rest defence at set pieces
points.text: How many outfield players stay behind halfway on attacking corners and free kicks?

points.label: Inter-line distance
points.text: Does the gap between midfield and defence exceed 12 metres during settled opponent possession?

name: Álvaro Arbeloa
source_file: Fulham Are Better Than You Think (Bains Analysis)

fullbacks.xp_impact: Robinson and Castagne push into the final third together for a 2-3-5, and Castagne jumps high onto opposing wing-backs; with both high, the centre-backs are isolated across the width

pivots.xp_impact: Berge drops between the split centre-backs as the main distributor; the Berge–Iwobi pivot lacks the recovery pace to cover after high turnovers

wingers.xp_impact: Iwobi drifts inside from the left to open the touchline for Robinson; on the right King underlaps into the box for cutbacks, rotating with Bobb and Castagne

strikers.xp_impact: Jiménez screens the central lane in the 4-2-3-1 press

points.label: Split centre-backs
points.text: Álvaro Arbeloa's Fulham build from the back with Calvin Bassey and Joachim Andersen split wide inside the box.

points.label: Both fullbacks high
points.text: Antonee Robinson and Timothy Castagne push into the opponent's third at the same time, forming a 2-3-5 / 2-2-6.

points.label: Right-side rotations
points.text: Castagne, Oscar Bobb and Josh King rotate on the right, with King underlapping into the box to create cutback angles.

points.label: High 4-2-3-1 press
points.text: Fulham press high, with Raúl Jiménez screening the central lane and King covering the holding midfielder.

points.label: Fullback jumps
points.text: When the ball goes wide, Castagne jumps high onto the opposing wing-back to pin them in their corner.

points.label: Carrying around the press
points.text: In build-up, rather than going long or forcing central passes, Bassey drives forward into the opposition half to beat the first line.

analysis.heading: In possession: box penetration and rotations

points.label: Box presence
points.text: Near the top of the league for touches in the opposition box, generating high open-play xG.

points.label: Inverted wing play
points.text: Alex Iwobi drifts inside from the left into the central attacking channel, opening the touchline for Robinson to overlap.

points.label: Short circulation
points.text: Sander Berge drops between the wide centre-backs as the main distributor, keeping the ball moving quickly.

points.label: Isolated centre-backs
points.text: With both fullbacks high, Andersen and Bassey are left covering about 60 metres of width; transitions into the channel behind Castagne exploit it.

points.label: Midfield ground coverage
points.text: The Berge–Iwobi pivot lacks the recovery pace to cover big spaces after turnovers high up the pitch.

points.label: Fullback rest defence
points.text: Does one fullback stay back for a 3+2 rest defence, or do both go beyond the midfield line?

points.label: Bassey's carries
points.text: Track the success rate of Bassey's dribbles out of the defensive third under high pressure.

points.label: Box-entry types
points.text: Split Fulham's box entries into low cutbacks, wide overloads and aerial crosses.

name: Sergej Jakirović
source_file: Why The Premier League Is So EASY For Hull City (The Adam Clery Football Channel)

pivots.xp_impact: Two central midfielders stay compact in front of the back five and jump onto receivers baited into the pocket between the lines; going long to McBurnie keeps them from being dragged out of shape

strikers.xp_impact: McBurnie is the direct outlet — he drifts into the wide channels to contest aerial and physical duels against fullbacks, with teammates collecting the knockdowns

wingers.xp_impact: Lock onto the knockdown zones around McBurnie to win possession high; tuck inside when defending, which leaves the far touchline exposed

fullbacks.xp_impact: Defend narrow in the back five and concede the flanks to invite crosses; exposed 1v1 by fast switches before the line shifts

analysis.heading: Out of possession: the deliberately decompacted block

points.label: Base 5-4-1
points.text: A low-to-mid 5-4-1 block, a move away from the 4-2-3-1 used in the Championship.

points.label: Baiting space between the lines
points.text: Hull deliberately leave gaps between the defensive and midfield lines, inviting the ball carrier to play into the interior corridor rather than circulate around the block.

points.label: Synchronised jumping
points.text: Once an opponent plays into that central pocket, the back five or the midfield pivot jump together to collapse onto the receiver, with teammates covering immediately behind.

analysis.heading: Funnelling to the flanks: aerial superiority traps

points.label: Central congestion
points.text: Three centre-backs (John Egan, Semi Ajayi, Noble Mendy) and two central midfielders stay compact inside the box, forcing attacks out wide.

points.label: Cross domination
points.text: Hull concede the flanks on purpose to draw high cross volumes — 34 crosses faced against Coventry, 39 against Manchester United. Egan and Ajayi win 60–70%+ of their ground and aerial duels, clearing the first ball before a good chance develops.

points.label: Direct over the block
points.text: In transition Hull skip midfield circulation entirely and go straight to Ollie McBurnie.

points.label: Target isolation in wide channels
points.text: McBurnie leaves the central corridor to contest duels against opposing fullbacks out wide. That keeps Hull's midfielders in shape and stops clearances coming straight back toward goal.

points.label: Second balls
points.text: Wingers and midfielders crowd the knockdown zones around McBurnie to secure possession in advanced areas.

points.label: Rapid switches
points.text: Defending narrow with a back five and tucked-in wide midfielders leaves the far touchline open. Quick switches that avoid McBurnie's channel pressure can isolate a wing-back 1v1 before the line shifts.

points.label: Low cutbacks
points.text: High crosses play into Hull's aerial strength. Low cutbacks to the edge of the area — the space vacated by retreating centre-backs — exploit the gap in front of the five-man line.

name: Gary O'Neil
source_file: How Ipswich Setup Under Gary O’Neil 🚜

pivots.rotation_risk_factors: High aggressive ball-winning demand in double pivot

strikers.xp_impact: Striker acts as central reference point for long balls & hold-up

name: Daniel Farke
source_file: Why Every Premier League Club Should Fear This Leeds Team. (Jacob Horsfall)

fullbacks.xp_impact: Bogle inverts from right wing-back into the #10 pocket, drawing centre-backs out; James Justin overlaps from right centre-back, which leaves the right side open on turnovers

pivots.xp_impact: Ampadu anchors a 3-1 base with Trafford as a third centre-back, and forms a central triangle with Tanaka and Stach out of possession; balls over the triangle find the space behind him

strikers.xp_impact: Calvert-Lewin occupies the centre-backs and is the diagonal outlet under pressure, with midfielders surrounding the drop zone

wingers.xp_impact: Okafor pins the far side and makes blind-side runs to the far post for crosses

points.label: Keeper as a third centre-back
points.text: Daniel Farke's Leeds build asymmetrically: goalkeeper James Trafford joins the two centre-backs and Ethan Ampadu to form a 3-1 base.

points.label: Overlapping centre-back
points.text: Right centre-back James Justin pushes into the right wing or attacking midfield, while right wing-back Jayden Bogle inverts into the #10 pocket, dragging centre-backs out of position.

points.label: Left-side isolation
points.text: With the right overloaded, Noah Okafor and Dominic Calvert-Lewin pin the defence on the far side, opening space for Anton Stach to attack the box.

points.label: Split press
points.text: Calvert-Lewin and Okafor split the centre-backs, blocking angles into the fullbacks without lunging at the ball carrier.

points.label: Central jamming
points.text: Ampadu, Ao Tanaka and Stach form a compact central triangle in a mid-block, forcing play into wide traps.

points.label: Touchline traps
points.text: Once the ball reaches an opposing fullback, the wing-back jumps aggressively with the near-side midfielder in support, forcing a turnover or a hurried clearance.

analysis.heading: In possession: counter-movements and box overloads

points.label: Suck and release
points.text: Bogle drives inside to draw three defenders, lays off to Stach, who spreads it to Justin in wide space.

points.label: Blind-side runs
points.text: Calvert-Lewin occupies the centre-backs, freeing Okafor to run blind-side to the far post for crosses.

points.label: Controlled long balls
points.text: Under heavy pressure Leeds hit targeted diagonals to Calvert-Lewin and surround the drop zone with midfielders to win the second ball.

points.label: Right side on turnovers
points.text: Justin's advanced position leaves the right side of defence open; quick switches can isolate the two remaining centre-backs.

points.label: Over the midfield triangle
points.text: Direct aerial balls over the central triangle exploit the space behind Ampadu.

points.label: Bogle's inversion
points.text: How much time does Bogle spend in the #10 pocket compared with touches on the right touchline?

points.label: Rest defence
points.text: Do Ampadu and Trafford form a two-man screen behind the remaining centre-backs during deep possession?

points.label: Second balls
points.text: What share of Calvert-Lewin's knockdowns do Stach or Tanaka win in the middle third?

name: Andoni Iraola
source_file: How Iraola's Liverpool will get better (The Athletic FC)

strikers.xp_impact: Isak arcs his press at the goalkeeper, blocking the switch and forcing the ball to one centre-back — the trigger for the chain of jumps behind him

pivots.xp_impact: Mac Allister, Morton or Gravenberch drop between defenders to receive on the half-turn; Szoboszlai steps up to cover the near-side pivot in the press

fullbacks.xp_impact: Kerkez and Barcola jump onto opposing fullbacks to intercept clearances and hurried sideline passes

wingers.xp_impact: Pin the opposing fullbacks wide while the midfield staggers between the lines

points.label: Zonal base, man-to-man jumps
points.text: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool set up nominally in a zonal 4-2-3-1 / 4-3-3 but jump into man-to-man assignments as the ball moves.

points.label: Compressing the pocket
points.text: When opposing playmakers drop deep, centre-backs such as Jérémy Jacquet step into midfield to squeeze the space between the lines.

points.label: Accordion build-up
points.text: In possession the ball goes back to Alisson to draw the opponent out, opening vertical space between their forwards and midfield.

points.label: Arc-run trigger
points.text: Alexander Isak curves his run at the goalkeeper, blocking the switch and forcing the ball toward one centre-back.

points.label: Chain-reaction jumps
points.text: Isak's run triggers Florian Wirtz to jump onto the other centre-back, while Dominik Szoboszlai steps up onto the near-side pivot.

points.label: Fullback interceptions
points.text: Milos Kerkez and Bradley Barcola jump onto the opposing fullbacks to intercept clearances or hurried sideline passes.

points.label: Runs from deep
points.text: Vertical runs from deep positions are the main way Liverpool break a block.

points.label: Line staggering
points.text: Midfielders (Alexis Mac Allister, Tyler Morton or Ryan Gravenberch) drop between defenders to receive on the half-turn while the wingers pin the fullbacks wide.

points.label: Bounce passes
points.text: One-touch wall passes in the half-spaces bypass the opponent's pressing lines.

points.label: Late second-line jumps
points.text: If the second presser (e.g. Wirtz) hesitates, the ball carrier has time to find midfield runners.

points.label: Overcommitting to inside runners
points.text: When several defenders track an inverted winger, the opposing fullback is left free on the far side for a switch.

points.label: Wirtz's timing
points.text: How long between Isak's run and Wirtz closing down the other centre-back?

points.label: Van Dijk stepping out
points.text: How often does Virgil van Dijk step out of the line into midfield versus holding depth?

points.label: First-touch direction
points.text: In build-up, do the midfielders take their first touch forward into space or back toward the centre-backs?

name: Enzo Maresca
source_file: The Problem with City's Press | Man City 5-3 Sunderland Analysis (LNobbins)

fullbacks.xp_impact: Gvardiol jumps into the attacking third to mark the opposing right-back when Semenyo presses, leaving a gap in City's left half-space; in possession he underlaps into the box for low crosses

pivots.xp_impact: Anderson and Enzo Fernández get pulled apart — Anderson presses forward, Enzo drops into the back line — vacating the central corridor

strikers.xp_impact: Haaland curves his press at the goalkeeper to block the near centre-back and funnel play to one flank; the target for Donnarumma's long distribution

wingers.xp_impact: Semenyo, Cherki and Ndiaye rotate across the front line for 1v1 dribbles and shooting lanes in the box

analysis.heading: Structure: the jumping fullback and an overextended press

points.label: 4-3-3 into man-to-man
points.text: Enzo Maresca sets City up in a man-marking high press, each player locked onto an opponent. Erling Haaland curves his run at the goalkeeper while blocking the pass to the near centre-back.

points.label: Asymmetric left-back
points.text: Joško Gvardiol jumps into the attacking third to mark the opposing right-back whenever Antoine Semenyo presses high, leaving a big gap behind him in the left half-space.

points.label: Midfield disconnect
points.text: With no natural holding pivot, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández get pulled apart: Anderson presses aggressively while Enzo drops into the back line, vacating the centre.

points.label: Curved-run trigger
points.text: The press starts when the opposing goalkeeper receives, with Haaland's angle of approach funnelling the ball to one flank.

points.label: Cover-shadow failures
points.text: Midfielders repeatedly fail to keep opponents in their cover shadow, watching the ball instead of the runners behind them.

points.label: Extreme high line
points.text: The back line steps up near halfway to compress space but doesn't pressure the passer, so timed runs beat the offside trap.

analysis.heading: In possession: overloads and final-third power

points.label: More direct
points.text: City build more vertically, with Gianluigi Donnarumma going long to Haaland to bypass midfield pressing.

points.label: Front-line rotations
points.text: Semenyo, Rayan Cherki and Iliman Ndiaye rotate across the front line, creating 1v1 dribbles and shooting lanes in the box.

points.label: Weak-side underlap
points.text: As play condenses on the right, Gvardiol underlaps into the box to put low crosses across goal.

points.label: The Gvardiol channel
points.text: Early passes into the space Gvardiol vacates bypass City's high line.

points.label: Central corridor
points.text: When Anderson lunges forward, a first-time bounce pass to an interior runner takes City's whole midfield out.

points.label: Gvardiol's recovery runs
points.text: How long does he take to recover when he has jumped forward and a vertical pass goes into his channel?

points.label: Rest-defence numbers
points.text: Does City keep a 3+1 rest defence, or leave the two centre-backs isolated 2v2?

points.label: Central bypasses
points.text: Count how often Enzo Fernández or Anderson are bypassed by forward passes from the opponent's defensive third.

name: Michael Carrick
source_file: Why Michael Carrick's Man United ISN'T Working (The Adam Clery Football Channel)

pivots.xp_impact: Mainoo and Tielemans step to passes after they are struck rather than anticipating, and hold no cover shadow — opponents pass straight through the double pivot

fullbacks.xp_impact: Advance high; with little counter-pressing behind them, opposing runners attack the space they leave in transition

analysis.heading: Structure: the chasm between the lines

points.label: Passive mid-block
points.text: Michael Carrick's United defend in a 4-2-3-1 / 4-4-2, but the vertical gap between the back line and the double pivot is far too large.

points.label: No compact funnelling
points.text: When pressing toward the touchline, United don't slide across as a unit. Instead of an overload they are left 5v4 down on the ball side, opening interior passing lanes.

points.label: Hesitant back line
points.text: When the opposing striker drops, the centre-backs hold position instead of tracking him, leaving room to turn unchallenged.

points.label: Reactive stepping
points.text: Midfielders such as Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans react once a pass is struck rather than moving while it travels, arriving late to challenges.

points.label: Unscreened centre
points.text: Opponents pass straight through the double pivot because neither midfielder sets an active cover shadow.

points.label: Slow recovery
points.text: Once the first line is bypassed, tracking back is slow, stranding the back four in open 4v4s on the halfway line.

points.label: Better without the ball
points.text: United take 2.66 points per game with under 50% possession, living off counterattacks, but only 1.6 with over 50%.

points.label: No half-space operator
points.text: There is no genuine interior playmaker who thrives in the tight space between the opposition's midfield and defence.

points.label: Bruno drops deep
points.text: Bruno Fernandes drops into the defensive third, onto the centre-backs' toes, to play from deep — leaving the central pocket empty and the low block unthreatened.

points.label: Central corridor
points.text: Opponents progress repeatedly with ground passes through the gaps between United's central midfielders.

points.label: Isolated fullbacks in transition
points.text: With no effective counter-press, runners exploit the space behind the advancing fullbacks to create quick overloads.

name: Matthias Jaissle
source_file: Why Newcastle's Fast Start Changed EVERYTHING Against Hull (A Game Of Two Halves)

pivots.xp_impact: Neave-Stir anchors as a lone pivot dictating tempo; when he went off injured, the reshuffle cost central ball retention and Newcastle conceded 21 shots

fullbacks.xp_impact: Miley tucks in from right-back to help build-up and rest defence; Hall overlaps for width on the left and steps in front of target men to win long balls

wingers.xp_impact: Barnes cuts inside and carries through the inside-left channel, drawing centre-backs before slipping reverse passes to Willock and Hall

strikers.xp_impact: Fernández-Pardo presses several defenders in a row, forcing rushed clearances into touch

analysis.heading: Structure: single-pivot 4-3-3 and an inverted fullback

points.label: Asymmetric 4-3-3
points.text: Matthias Jaissle moved Newcastle from a 4-2-4 to a 4-3-3 against Hull's low block, with 18-year-old Sean Neave-Stir anchoring as a lone pivot, dictating tempo.

points.label: Inverted right-back
points.text: Lewis Miley moved from central midfield to right-back, tucking into inside pockets to help build-up and secure rest defence.

points.label: Left-side fluidity
points.text: Joe Willock dropped into the left half-space, Harvey Barnes cut inside toward the box, and left-back Lewis Hall overlapped for outside width.

points.label: Fast start
points.text: Newcastle opened with high-intensity pressing to disrupt Hull before their 5-4-1 block could settle.

points.label: Attacking the target man
points.text: When Hull went long to Ollie McBurnie, Hall stepped in front to win the ball before it reached him.

points.label: Chain pressing
points.text: Striker Fernández-Pardo pressed several defenders back-to-back, forcing rushed clearances into touch.

analysis.heading: In possession: rest defence and half-space combinations

points.label: Winning loose balls
points.text: Newcastle kept their rest defence high to win 50/50s outside Hull's box after blocked shots, keeping attacks alive in the final third.

points.label: Carry and release
points.text: Barnes carried through the inside-left channel, drew centre-backs, and slipped reverse passes to runners (Willock, Hall) for both opening goals.

points.label: Losing the pivot
points.text: When Neave-Stir went off injured, moving Miley back into midfield and Malick Thiaw to right-back broke the spacing: Newcastle lost central retention and conceded 21 shots.

points.label: Under a high press
points.text: When opponents press the back line hard, there are no rehearsed escape routes, so Newcastle resort to hurried long balls.

points.label: Rest-defence reactions
points.text: How quickly do Miley or Hall contest loose clearances outside the opponent's box?

points.label: Barnes' releases
points.text: Count Barnes' passes from the inside-left channel to runners breaking into the box.

points.label: Pivot retention
points.text: What is Neave-Stir's pass completion under direct pressure in the central third?

name: Oliver Glasner
source_file: I Analysed Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest System (The Villans)

fullbacks.xp_impact: Williams and Aina provide nearly all of Forest's width, with Williams the target for Murillo's diagonals; fast switches drag the outside centre-backs wide

pivots.xp_impact: Schlager and McAtee often sit on the same line, leaving pockets either side of them; Schlager plays vertical passes into Gibbs-White on the half-turn

wingers.xp_impact: Gibbs-White and Ndoye play narrow as twin #10s, run beyond Delap when he drops, and fall into a flat midfield four without the ball

strikers.xp_impact: Delap drops into midfield facing his own goal to pull a centre-back forward for the runners behind him

analysis.heading: Structure: narrow 5-2-2-1 and a flat midfield pair

points.label: Base 5-2-2-1
points.text: Oliver Glasner's Forest play a 5-2-2-1 that becomes a 5-4-1 or 5-3-2 without the ball: centre-backs Murillo, Nikola Milenković and Morato/Cunha, with wing-backs Neco Williams and Ola Aina.

points.label: Unstaggered pivot
points.text: Xaver Schlager and James McAtee often occupy the same horizontal line in average-position data, opening big pockets either side of the pair.

points.label: Narrow attack
points.text: The two #10s, Morgan Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye, play very narrow, concentrating play centrally and leaving the width almost entirely to the wing-backs.

points.label: Centre-back stepping
points.text: When an opposing playmaker receives in the pocket, Milenković steps out of the back three to challenge — and if he misses, space opens straight behind him.

points.label: 5-4-1 reshuffle
points.text: Holding shape, Gibbs-White and Ndoye drop wide into a flat midfield four to protect the half-spaces.

analysis.heading: In possession: striker drops and runners beyond

points.label: The false-target drop
points.text: Liam Delap drops into the midfield line facing his own goal, pulling a centre-back forward.

points.label: Runs beyond
points.text: As Delap drops, Gibbs-White and Ndoye run beyond him together into the vacated central space.

points.label: Progression routes
points.text: Forest progress with direct diagonals from Murillo out to Williams, or vertical passes from Schlager into Gibbs-White on the half-turn.

points.label: Either side of the midfield two
points.text: A three-man midfield or inverted wingers can exploit the space outside Schlager and McAtee.

points.label: Stretching the back five
points.text: Fast switches force the back line to slide, pulling the outside centre-backs into wide coverage.

points.label: Pivot staggering
points.text: In settled defence, how far apart vertically are Schlager and McAtee — and how often are they on the same line?

points.label: Delap's drops
points.text: How often does Delap drop to the centre circle, and does a midfield runner go beyond him when he does?

points.label: Milenković stepping out
points.text: What's his success rate when he steps out of the line to challenge interior receivers?

name: Régis Le Bris
source_file: Man City vs Sunderland (5-3) — Brobbey Was The Key — Tactical Analysis — GW6 FPL Info 26/27 (Steven Doherty)

strikers.xp_impact: Brobbey is the route-one target — Roefs goes long to him, and he pins centre-backs and cushions layoffs to Le Fée or Sadiki

fullbacks.xp_impact: Methalie and Mukiele make diagonal runs into central midfield; when they push high, switches leave the wide centre-backs 1v1

pivots.xp_impact: Sadiki and Xhaka sit behind the opponent's press to collect knockdowns from long balls

wingers.xp_impact: Angulo or Muñoz are released by Le Fée into the channels behind advancing fullbacks

points.label: Base 5-3-2
points.text: Régis Le Bris sets Sunderland up in a 5-3-2 out of possession that becomes a 3-4-1-2 / 3-4-3 going forward.

points.label: Stretching the pitch
points.text: Centre-backs drop deep in their own third to draw the opponent's press high, stretching the central corridor and leaving Brian Brobbey 1v1 with a centre-back.

points.label: Wing-backs come inside
points.text: Wing-backs Dayann Methalie and Nordi Mukiele make diagonal runs into central midfield, pulling defenders out of position.

points.label: Deliberate deep possession
points.text: Defenders circulate slowly near their own box to bait the opponent into committing numbers forward.

points.label: Second-ball positioning
points.text: Noah Sadiki and Granit Xhaka position themselves behind the opponent's press, ready to collect knockdowns from long balls.

analysis.heading: In possession: the route-one target engine

points.label: Direct to Brobbey
points.text: Goalkeeper Robin Roefs bypasses midfield with direct balls into Brobbey.

points.label: Hold-up and layoffs
points.text: Brobbey pins centre-backs with his frame and cushions aerial balls down to runners such as Enzo Le Fée or Sadiki.

points.label: Third-man release
points.text: Once the ball is secured centrally, Le Fée releases wingers Nilson Angulo or Chema Muñoz into the channels behind advancing fullbacks.

points.label: Space behind the wing-backs
points.text: With the wing-backs high, direct switches to opposing wingers leave the wide centre-backs 1v1.

points.label: Set-piece marking
points.text: Lapses tracking runners on quick restarts leave open shooting lanes in the box.

points.label: Brobbey's duels
points.text: Track his aerial and ground duel success in the middle third during the first half.

points.label: Le Fée facing forward
points.text: Count passes Le Fée receives facing forward after Brobbey's hold-up play.

points.label: Wing-back recovery
points.text: How long do Methalie and Mukiele take to drop into a back five after a turnover in the opposition half?

name: Roberto De Zerbi
source_file: Why De Zerbi's Tottenham Have Started The Season SO Badly (The Adam Clery Football Channel)

pivots.xp_impact: Tonali anchors as a single or double pivot but often mistimes his steps, leaving space in front of the centre-backs — and has to cover wide when the fullbacks are caught high

fullbacks.xp_impact: Push high in possession; direct balls into the channels behind them bypass the press

strikers.xp_impact: Part of the league's highest pressing-sequence volume, but only ~5% of high turnovers become shots for lack of supporting runs and angles

analysis.heading: Structure: vertical compression vs defensive disconnect

points.label: Stretched build-up
points.text: Roberto De Zerbi sets Tottenham up to hold the ball high and bait the opponent's press before playing through the central lines.

points.label: Broken pivot screen
points.text: Sandro Tonali anchors as a single or double pivot but often mistimes his steps. Big distances open between the pressing forwards and the back line, leaving space in front of the centre-backs.

points.label: Overextended fullbacks
points.text: The fullbacks push high, so the defensive midfielder has to cover wide areas whenever the ball is lost.

points.label: High pressing volume
points.text: First in the league for pressing sequences and fifth for high turnovers — Tottenham hunt the ball in the opponent's defensive third.

points.label: No decisive support
points.text: After winning the ball high, forward options lack supporting angles and timing: only about 5% of those turnovers end in a shot.

points.label: Edge of the box unprotected
points.text: In settled defence, midfielders watch the ball instead of tracking runners into the arc, conceding open shooting lanes.

points.label: Low-xG shots
points.text: Territorial control without coordinated box entries leads to speculative long-range shots rather than high-probability cutbacks.

points.label: No central ball carrying
points.text: The midfield rarely carries through a congested block, so circulation stays on the predictable perimeter.

points.label: Balls over the high line
points.text: Opponents bypass the front press with direct passes into the wide channels behind the advanced fullbacks.

points.label: Space behind Tonali
points.text: Midfield runners driving through the centre exploit the gap between Tottenham's midfield and retreating centre-backs.
